BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` — one file per detailed inline comment **Inline comment lines must be present in the PR diff.** GitHub review threads can only be attached to added or context lines inside a diff hunk. If `pr_diff.txt` is truncated, run `git diff origin/{baseBranch}...HEAD` to locate the correct line numbers. Findings on unchanged code outside the diff belong in `outputs/pr_review_general.md`, not as inline comments. Do NOT write `outputs/response.md`; the review is posted to GitHub only. ```mermaid flowchart TD O1["Write outputs/pr_review.json — structured data for GitHub PR review…

5:# by `ai-teammate`. Human-created issues (even labeled/assigned to the
6:# agent) do NOT trigger anything yet; that gate opens in a later phase.

9:#   issue labeled while assigned     → factory, leg derived by the guard
10:#   PR opened by ai-teammate         → factory, leg=review on the linked
11:#                                      issue (parsed from the PR body)
12:#   workflow_dispatch (SM / manual)  → leg pinned by input

14:# ALL loop logic lives in IstiN/dmtools-agents/.github/workflows/
15:# factory-teammate.yml (guard, legs, verdict, sessions, memory). This file

18:# per-issue concurrency group, and the call itself.

          # branch) diffs to nothing and the narrowed arms skip. A failed
          # resolve fails SAFE: both arms run unconditioned —
          # over-triggering a rare-path leg costs minutes, under-triggering
          # one hides a nightly-only red (the #1309 class).
          if [ -z "$HEAD_REF" ]; then
            HEAD_REF="$(git rev-parse HEAD)"
            BASE_REF="$(git merge-base origin/main "$HEAD_REF" 2>/dev/null || true)"
            if [ -z "$BASE_REF" ]; then
              echo "::warning::merge-base(origin/main, HEAD) failed on the dispatch checkout — failing safe: exzone + locksmoke arms run"
              echo "exzone=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
              echo "locksmoke=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
              echo "installer=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
              exit 0
            fi
          fi
          # Issue #1267 N1: the macOS exclusion-zone path set. Gated on
          # BOTH pull_request events and SM validation dispatches (the
          # legs below consult these outputs on either event). Context:
          # the ubuntu flutter-tests leg runs this family but every
          # engine-dependent test SKIPS there (native_test_guard.dart finds
          # no QuickJS .so on a bare runner); they truly execute only on
          # macOS — the hole #1309 escaped through (gh-1307). The issue's
          # packages/js_widget_runtime/** is an EXTERNAL repo now, so its
          # bumps arrive via the flutter_app/pubspec.yaml pin.
          if git diff --name-only "$BASE_REF" "$HEAD_REF" |
              grep -qE '(^flutter_app/lib/apps/|^lib/src/js_ext/|^flutter_app/test/apps/|^flutter_app/test/native_test_guard\.dart$|^flutter_app/pubspec\.yaml$)'; then
            echo "exzone=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi
          # Issue #1267 N2 (AC2): the lockfile-refresh vector — resolution
          # floats transitive deps to latest-compatible, and the breaking
          # arrival (#1265: a transitive flutter_inappwebview) lands as a
          # flutter_app/pubspec.lock diff with nothing else changed. The
          # flutter-app-lock-smoke legs are the pre-merge net; PRs not
          # touching the lockfile never pay for them.
          if git diff --name-only "$BASE_REF" "$HEAD_REF" |
              grep -qE '^flutter_app/pubspec\.lock$'; then
            echo "locksmoke=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi
          # gh-1596 REG-1/REG-2: the installer generation pipeline — every
          # sh artifact under site/ and the generator that renders them.
          # Gated on the SAME two events as exzone/locksmoke (pull_request
          # + validation dispatch); the classifier failure arm above runs
          # it fail-safe.
          if git diff --name-only "$BASE_REF" "$HEAD_REF" |
              grep -qE '(^site/|^scripts/gen_installers\.dart$)'; then
            echo "installer=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi
          if [ "${{ github.event_name }}" != "pull_request" ]; then
            # Dispatch done — the stages classifier below reads a
            # pull_request event's base/head only; on dispatches the group
            # outputs stay with the non-PR filter step (full gate).
            exit 0
          fi
          stages=$(scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh --dry-run |
            sed -n 's/^Fast gate scope: .*stages://p')
          echo "gate stages:[$stages]"

          [ -z "$(echo $stages)" ] && stages="size analyze test-core coverage crap dup dupx flutter integration-mock"
          case " $stages " in *"flutter"*) echo "app=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT" ;; esac
          case " $stages " in *"test-core"*) echo "core=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT" ;; esac
          case " $stages " in *"analyze"*) echo "docs=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT" ;; esac
          # Issue #551: test/integration changes select the mock-LLM leg.
          case " $stages " in *"integration-mock"*) echo "intmock=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT" ;; esac
          # All nine stages selected = a shared/unknown path changed:
          if [ -z "$(echo $stages)" ]; then
            # Empty output can only mean detection failure: full gate.

          fi

          fi

          # trajectory regressions, not only the release — before #551 the
          # only integration leg outside PRs was tag-time. The perf-gate
          # leg re-selects the same gate via --tags perf. Paths = everything
          # the #262 fix touched: ledger core, fa_ui trajectory widgets, CLI
          # trajectory parts, the fah entrypoint, its tests, and the app's
          # session load path.
          if git diff --name-only "$BASE_REF" "$HEAD_REF" |

          # model_request_summary records and the session chain's shape —
          # a red usage-fold suite blocks the merge even when the regular
          # legs are green.
          if git diff --name-only "$BASE_REF" "$HEAD_REF" |
              grep -qE '(^lib/src/trajectory/|^lib/src/session/|^lib/src/usage/|^test/usage/|^lib/src/cli/agent_cli_usage_ledger\.dart$)'; then
            echo "usagefold=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

78:  contents: read

80:concurrency:
81:  # PR-anchored dispatches (#544/#687) carry no issue — fall back to the pr
82:  # input so each PR keeps its OWN group ('ai-teammate-issue-pr-266');
83:  # without it every PR-anchored run shares the empty group and serializes

85:  group: ai-teammate-issue-${{ github.event.issue.number || github.event.inputs.issue || format('pr-{0}', github.event.inputs.pr) }}

91:  # exits empty and the factory job is skipped. PRs do NOT trigger this
92:  # workflow: the loop's review/rework legs are driven by SM ticks and
93:  # issue labels, and pull_request-triggered runs of this stub validated

95:  gate:

135:                  --jq '[.assignees[].login] | map(select(. != "ai-teammate")) | length')
136:                if [ "$HUMAN" = "0" ]; then
137:                  echo "leg=dev" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
138:                else
139:                  echo "leg=" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
140:                  echo "::notice title=machine-standby::issue #${ISSUE_NUMBER} has a human assignee — no dev, review-only"
141:                fi
142:              else
143:                echo "leg=" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
144:              fi
145:              echo "issue=${ISSUE_NUMBER}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
146:              ;;
147:          esac
148:          echo "→ gate done (see outputs)"

150:  factory:
151:    needs: gate
152:    # Dispatch runs carry the target in inputs (gate outputs are empty by
153:    # design there); event runs carry it in gate outputs.
154:    if: needs.gate.result == 'success' && (needs.gate.outputs.issue != '' || github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch')
155:    # Job-scoped grants mirroring the pinned callee's declared scopes (a
156:    # reusable call is capped by the calling job's effective permissions —

158:    # this workflow defaults to the top-level read-only.

          # branch) diffs to nothing and the narrowed arms skip. A failed
          # resolve fails SAFE: both arms run unconditioned —

          # one hides a nightly-only red (the #1309 class).

            HEAD_REF="$(git rev-parse HEAD)"
            BASE_REF="$(git merge-base origin/main "$HEAD_REF" 2>/dev/null || true)"
            if [ -z "$BASE_REF" ]; then
              echo "::warning::merge-base(origin/main, HEAD) failed on the dispatch checkout — failing safe: exzone + locksmoke arms run"
              echo "exzone=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
              echo "locksmoke=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
              echo "installer=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
              exit 0
            fi
          fi
          # Issue #1267 N1: the macOS exclusion-zone path set. Gated on
          # BOTH pull_request events and SM validation dispatches (the
          # legs below consult these outputs on either event). Context:
          # the ubuntu flutter-tests leg runs this family but every
          # engine-dependent test SKIPS there (native_test_guard.dart finds
          # no QuickJS .so on a bare runner); they truly execute only on
          # macOS — the hole #1309 escaped through (gh-1307). The issue's
          # packages/js_widget_runtime/** is an EXTERNAL repo now, so its
          # bumps arrive via the flutter_app/pubspec.yaml pin.
          if git diff --name-only "$BASE_REF" "$HEAD_REF" |
              grep -qE '(^flutter_app/lib/apps/|^lib/src/js_ext/|^flutter_app/test/apps/|^flutter_app/test/native_test_guard\.dart$|^flutter_app/pubspec\.yaml$)'; then
            echo "exzone=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

          # Issue #1267 N2 (AC2): the lockfile-refresh vector — resolution
          # floats transitive deps to latest-compatible, and the breaking
          # arrival (#1265: a transitive flutter_inappwebview) lands as a
          # flutter_app/pubspec.lock diff with nothing else changed. The
          # flutter-app-lock-smoke legs are the pre-merge net; PRs not
          # touching the lockfile never pay for them.
          if git diff --name-only "$BASE_REF" "$HEAD_REF" |
              grep -qE '^flutter_app/pubspec\.lock$'; then

          # sh artifact under site/ and the generator that renders them.

          if git diff --name-only "$BASE_REF" "$HEAD_REF" |

stage_integration_mock() {
  # Issue #551: the no-key integration legs run on EVERY PR that touches
  # them — MockLlmServer scenarios, no secrets, no network, so they cannot
  # rot silently between releases (#538 class). Real-provider files carry
  # the `llm` tag and stay in the tag-only smoke job; browser-ext owns its
  # own workflow; perf has the #303 per-PR trajectory gate; `pty` marks
  # child-agent-spawn tests (issue #553) — nightly-only, unbounded boot time.
  #
  # TMPDIR normalization (macOS hook parity): several PTY legs assert the
  # status row still shows `· ctx ` — with macOS's per-user temp root
  # (/var/folders/<30 chars>/T/...) the temp cwd eats the whole row width
  # and the assertion fails locally while ubuntu CI (/tmp) is green. Pin
  # the stage to the same short temp root CI has so hook/CI agree.
  echo "🧪 Running no-key integration legs (MockLlmServer)..."
  local conc="${FA_DART_TEST_CONCURRENCY:-$(detect_test_concurrency)}"
  echo "   concurrency: ${conc:-default}"
  #
  # Flake budget (gh-1026): FA_GATE_PTY_RETRIES=N reruns ONLY the failed
  # files, up to N times, before the stage fails. The PTY/grid timing legs
  # are load-sensitive (the gh-1026 class: 3 red 2.5 h gate runs on an
  # unchanged head, a different ambient test red each time, every file
  # green in isolation) — the budget turns one flaky PTY case from a full
  # leg rerun into a minutes-scoped file rerun, mirroring CI's
  # retrigger-recovery behaviour (ci.yml watchdog: ONE retrigger, never a
  # blind rerun). 0 (the default) keeps the single-shot leg below
  # byte-identical. Files come from scripts/gate_failed_targets.py over
  # the dart json file-reporter log; when the log yields no targets
  # (crash before the reporter flushed) the stage fails WITHOUT a rerun —
  # never rerun blind.
  local retries="${FA_GATE_PTY_RETRIES:-0}"
  if [ "$retries" -le 0 ]; then
    TMPDIR="${FA_GATE_TMPDIR:-/tmp}" \
      dart test ${conc:+--concurrency=$conc} test/integration \
      --exclude-tags llm,browser-ext,perf,pty
    return
  fi
  local log="test-results/gate-integration-mock.json"
  mkdir -p test-results
  local targets="test/integration"
  local attempt=0
  while true; do
    attempt=$((attempt + 1))
    if TMPDIR="${FA_GATE_TMPDIR:-/tmp}" \
        dart test ${conc:+--concurrency=$conc} $targets \
        --exclude-tags llm,browser-ext,perf,pty \
        --file-reporter="json:$log"; then
      return 0
    fi
    if [ "$attempt" -gt "$retries" ]; then
      echo "❌ flake budget exhausted ($retries rerun(s)) — integration leg stays red" >&2
      exit 1
    fi
    local failed
    failed=$(python3 scripts/gate_failed_targets.py "$log")
    if [ -z "$failed" ]; then
      echo "   no failed-file targets in $log — not rerunning blind" >&2
      exit 1
    fi
    echo "🔁 flake budget: rerun $attempt/$retries — failed files only:" >&2
    printf '%s\n' "$failed" | sed 's/^/   /' >&2
    targets="$failed"
  done
}

59:        required: false
60:        type: string

72:# write): a reusable workflow cannot RAISE rights above the CALLING JOB's
73:# effective grant, so an explicit read-only block ON THE CALLING JOB made
74:# every call fail validation with startup_failure (live bisect,
75:# 2026-09-18) — the job-scoped mirror is the minimal consistent set (SEC-08,
76:# #796).

78:  contents: read
79:
80:concurrency:
81:  # PR-anchored dispatches (#544/#687) carry no issue — fall back to the pr
82:  # input so each PR keeps its OWN group ('ai-teammate-issue-pr-266');
83:  # without it every PR-anchored run shares the empty group and serializes
84:  # across unrelated PRs.
85:  group: ai-teammate-issue-${{ github.event.issue.number || github.event.inputs.issue || format('pr-{0}', github.event.inputs.pr) }}
86:  cancel-in-progress: false
87:
88:jobs:
89:  # Assignment gate. Runs ONLY when the issue is assigned to `ai-teammate`
90:  # (the human handoff) or on explicit dispatch (SM ticks). Everything else
91:  # exits empty and the factory job is skipped. PRs do NOT trigger this
92:  # workflow: the loop's review/rework legs are driven by SM ticks and
93:  # issue labels, and pull_request-triggered runs of this stub validated

101:    # It inherits the workflow-level read-only default and must NOT see the
102:    # factory job's write scopes (SEC-08 review, #796).
103:    permissions:
104:      contents: read
105:    outputs:
106:      issue: ${{ steps.resolve.outputs.issue }}
107:      leg: ${{ steps.resolve.outputs.leg }}
108:    steps:
109:      - name: Resolve target issue and leg for this event
110:        id: resolve
111:        env:
112:          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
113:          EVENT: ${{ github.event_name }}
114:          ACTION: ${{ github.event.action }}
115:          NUMBER: ${{ github.event.number }}
116:          ISSUE_NUMBER: ${{ github.event.issue.number }}

122:              echo "issue=${ISSUE_NUMBER}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"   # empty here; factory takes inputs.issue

127:              # handoff) → dev leg; `labeled` (agent:review / agent:rework
128:              # added by the machine itself while assigned) → guard derives.

132:              # review-external-once / agent:review on the eventual PR).
133:              if [ "$ACTION" = "assigned" ]; then
134:                HUMAN=$(gh api "repos/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/issues/${ISSUE_NUMBER}" \
135:                  --jq '[.assignees[].login] | map(select(. != "ai-teammate")) | length')
136:                if [ "$HUMAN" = "0" ]; then
137:                  echo "leg=dev" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
138:                else
139:                  echo "leg=" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
140:                  echo "::notice title=machine-standby::issue #${ISSUE_NUMBER} has a human assignee — no dev, review-only"
141:                fi
142:              else
143:                echo "leg=" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
144:              fi
145:              echo "issue=${ISSUE_NUMBER}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
146:              ;;
147:          esac
148:          echo "→ gate done (see outputs)"

150:  factory:
151:    needs: gate
152:    # Dispatch runs carry the target in inputs (gate outputs are empty by
153:    # design there); event runs carry it in gate outputs.
154:    if: needs.gate.result == 'success' && (needs.gate.outputs.issue != '' || github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch')
155:    # Job-scoped grants mirroring the pinned callee's declared scopes (a
156:    # reusable call is capped by the calling job's effective permissions —
157:    # see the top-level comment). Scoped to THIS job so any future job in
158:    # this workflow defaults to the top-level read-only.

            HEAD_REF="$(git rev-parse HEAD)"
            BASE_REF="$(git merge-base origin/main "$HEAD_REF" 2>/dev/null || true)"

              echo "::warning::merge-base(origin/main, HEAD) failed on the dispatch checkout — failing safe: exzone + locksmoke arms run"
              echo "exzone=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
              echo "locksmoke=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
              echo "installer=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

          # BOTH pull_request events and SM validation dispatches (the
          # legs below consult these outputs on either event). Context:
          # the ubuntu flutter-tests leg runs this family but every
          # engine-dependent test SKIPS there (native_test_guard.dart finds

          # packages/js_widget_runtime/** is an EXTERNAL repo now, so its
          # bumps arrive via the flutter_app/pubspec.yaml pin.
          if git diff --name-only "$BASE_REF" "$HEAD_REF" |
              grep -qE '(^flutter_app/lib/apps/|^lib/src/js_ext/|^flutter_app/test/apps/|^flutter_app/test/native_test_guard\.dart$|^flutter_app/pubspec\.yaml$)'; then

          # floats transitive deps to latest-compatible, and the breaking

          # flutter_app/pubspec.lock diff with nothing else changed. The

          if git diff --name-only "$BASE_REF" "$HEAD_REF" |

  # the stage to the same short temp root CI has so hook/CI agree.
  echo "🧪 Running no-key integration legs (MockLlmServer)..."
  local conc="${FA_DART_TEST_CONCURRENCY:-$(detect_test_concurrency)}"
  echo "   concurrency: ${conc:-default}"
  #
  # Flake budget (gh-1026): FA_GATE_PTY_RETRIES=N reruns ONLY the failed
  # files, up to N times, before the stage fails. The PTY/grid timing legs
  # are load-sensitive (the gh-1026 class: 3 red 2.5 h gate runs on an
  # unchanged head, a different ambient test red each time, every file
  # green in isolation) — the budget turns one flaky PTY case from a full
  # leg rerun into a minutes-scoped file rerun, mirroring CI's
  # retrigger-recovery behaviour (ci.yml watchdog: ONE retrigger, never a
  # blind rerun). 0 (the default) keeps the single-shot leg below
  # byte-identical. Files come from scripts/gate_failed_targets.py over
  # the dart json file-reporter log; when the log yields no targets
  # (crash before the reporter flushed) the stage fails WITHOUT a rerun —
  # never rerun blind.
  local retries="${FA_GATE_PTY_RETRIES:-0}"
  if [ "$retries" -le 0 ]; then
    TMPDIR="${FA_GATE_TMPDIR:-/tmp}" \
      dart test ${conc:+--concurrency=$conc} test/integration \
      --exclude-tags llm,browser-ext,perf,pty
    return
  fi
  local log="test-results/gate-integration-mock.json"
  mkdir -p test-results
  local targets="test/integration"
  local attempt=0
  while true; do
    attempt=$((attempt + 1))
    if TMPDIR="${FA_GATE_TMPDIR:-/tmp}" \
        dart test ${conc:+--concurrency=$conc} $targets \
        --exclude-tags llm,browser-ext,perf,pty \
        --file-reporter="json:$log"; then
      return 0
    fi
    if [ "$attempt" -gt "$retries" ]; then
      echo "❌ flake budget exhausted ($retries rerun(s)) — integration leg stays red" >&2
      exit 1
    fi
    local failed
    failed=$(python3 scripts/gate_failed_targets.py "$log")
    if [ -z "$failed" ]; then
      echo "   no failed-file targets in $log — not rerunning blind" >&2
      exit 1
    fi
    echo "🔁 flake budget: rerun $attempt/$retries — failed files only:" >&2
    printf '%s\n' "$failed" | sed 's/^/   /' >&2
    targets="$failed"
  done
}

137:                  echo "leg=dev" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
138:                else
139:                  echo "leg=" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
140:                  echo "::notice title=machine-standby::issue #${ISSUE_NUMBER} has a human assignee — no dev, review-only"
141:                fi
142:              else
143:                echo "leg=" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
144:              fi
145:              echo "issue=${ISSUE_NUMBER}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
146:              ;;
147:          esac
148:          echo "→ gate done (see outputs)"

150:  factory:
151:    needs: gate
152:    # Dispatch runs carry the target in inputs (gate outputs are empty by
153:    # design there); event runs carry it in gate outputs.
154:    if: needs.gate.result == 'success' && (needs.gate.outputs.issue != '' || github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch')

156:    # reusable call is capped by the calling job's effective permissions —

              echo "::warning::merge-base(origin/main, HEAD) failed on the dispatch checkout — failing safe: exzone + locksmoke arms run"
              echo "exzone=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
              echo "locksmoke=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
              echo "installer=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

          # BOTH pull_request events and SM validation dispatches (the
          # legs below consult these outputs on either event). Context:
          # the ubuntu flutter-tests leg runs this family but every
          # engine-dependent test SKIPS there (native_test_guard.dart finds

          # packages/js_widget_runtime/** is an EXTERNAL repo now, so its
          # bumps arrive via the flutter_app/pubspec.yaml pin.

              grep -qE '(^flutter_app/lib/apps/|^lib/src/js_ext/|^flutter_app/test/apps/|^flutter_app/test/native_test_guard\.dart$|^flutter_app/pubspec\.yaml$)'; then

          # floats transitive deps to latest-compatible, and the breaking
          # arrival (#1265: a transitive flutter_inappwebview) lands as a
          # flutter_app/pubspec.lock diff with nothing else changed. The

          if git diff --name-only "$BASE_REF" "$HEAD_REF" |

  # hits must ALSO reach the unit-side lcov consumers (>= 80% ratchet, PR
  # diff-coverage, CRAP: jsr_cli.dart at 0% line coverage reads CRAP 156
  # against the 12.0 ceiling), so the trio runs into the SAME coverage/
  # dir; format_coverage merges the per-isolate files. Keep this list in
  # sync with ci.yml (test-core shard 0); gh-1538 retired the nightly.yml
  # full-quality copy — the pre-merge gate is the single unit-lcov producer.
  dart test ${conc:+--concurrency=$conc} --tags integration \
    test/cli/jsr_cli_test.dart \
    test/cli/cli_args_jsr_test.dart \
    test/cli/agent_cli_jsr_test.dart \
    --coverage=coverage
}

stage_integration_mock() {
  # Issue #551: the no-key integration legs run on EVERY PR that touches
  # them — MockLlmServer scenarios, no secrets, no network, so they cannot
  # rot silently between releases (#538 class). Real-provider files carry
  # the `llm` tag and stay in the tag-only smoke job; browser-ext owns its
  # own workflow; perf has the #303 per-PR trajectory gate; `pty` marks
  # child-agent-spawn tests (issue #553) — nightly-only, unbounded boot time.
  #
  # TMPDIR normalization (macOS hook parity): several PTY legs assert the
  # status row still shows `· ctx ` — with macOS's per-user temp root
  # (/var/folders/<30 chars>/T/...) the temp cwd eats the whole row width
  # and the assertion fails locally while ubuntu CI (/tmp) is green. Pin
  # the stage to the same short temp root CI has so hook/CI agree.
  echo "🧪 Running no-key integration legs (MockLlmServer)..."
  local conc="${FA_DART_TEST_CONCURRENCY:-$(detect_test_concurrency)}"
  echo "   concurrency: ${conc:-default}"
  #
  # Flake budget (gh-1026): FA_GATE_PTY_RETRIES=N reruns ONLY the failed
  # files, up to N times, before the stage fails. The PTY/grid timing legs
  # are load-sensitive (the gh-1026 class: 3 red 2.5 h gate runs on an
  # unchanged head, a different ambient test red each time, every file
  # green in isolation) — the budget turns one flaky PTY case from a full
  # leg rerun into a minutes-scoped file rerun, mirroring CI's
  # retrigger-recovery behaviour (ci.yml watchdog: ONE retrigger, never a
  # blind rerun). 0 (the default) keeps the single-shot leg below
  # byte-identical. Files come from scripts/gate_failed_targets.py over
  # the dart json file-reporter log; when the log yields no targets
  # (crash before the reporter flushed) the stage fails WITHOUT a rerun —
  # never rerun blind.
  local retries="${FA_GATE_PTY_RETRIES:-0}"
  if [ "$retries" -le 0 ]; then
    TMPDIR="${FA_GATE_TMPDIR:-/tmp}" \
      dart test ${conc:+--concurrency=$conc} test/integration \
      --exclude-tags llm,browser-ext,perf,pty
    return
  fi
  local log="test-results/gate-integration-mock.json"
  mkdir -p test-results
  local targets="test/integration"
  local attempt=0
  while true; do
    attempt=$((attempt + 1))
    if TMPDIR="${FA_GATE_TMPDIR:-/tmp}" \
        dart test ${conc:+--concurrency=$conc} $targets \
        --exclude-tags llm,browser-ext,perf,pty \
        --file-reporter="json:$log"; then
      return 0
    fi
    if [ "$attempt" -gt "$retries" ]; then
      echo "❌ flake budget exhausted ($retries rerun(s)) — integration leg stays red" >&2
      exit 1
    fi
    local failed
    failed=$(python3 scripts/gate_failed_targets.py "$log")
    if [ -z "$failed" ]; then
      echo "   no failed-file targets in $log — not rerunning blind" >&2
      exit 1
    fi
    echo "🔁 flake budget: rerun $attempt/$retries — failed files only:" >&2
    printf '%s\n' "$failed" | sed 's/^/   /' >&2
    targets="$failed"
  done
}

              echo "exzone=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
              echo "locksmoke=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
              echo "installer=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

          # BOTH pull_request events and SM validation dispatches (the

stage_test_core() {
  echo "🧪 Running dart test --coverage (excluding integration tests)..."
  rm -rf coverage
  local conc="${FA_DART_TEST_CONCURRENCY:-$(detect_test_concurrency)}"
  echo "   concurrency: ${conc:-default}"
  dart test ${conc:+--concurrency=$conc} --coverage=coverage --exclude-tags integration
  # gh-1033 (review thread 7 + gate wiring): the fa jsr delegate suites are
  # integration-tagged — the PTY leg's CLI coverage ratchet measures
  # lib/src/cli hits from them — so the unit run above skips them. Their
  # hits must ALSO reach the unit-side lcov consumers (>= 80% ratchet, PR
  # diff-coverage, CRAP: jsr_cli.dart at 0% line coverage reads CRAP 156
  # against the 12.0 ceiling), so the trio runs into the SAME coverage/
  # dir; format_coverage merges the per-isolate files. Keep this list in
  # sync with ci.yml (test-core shard 0); gh-1538 retired the nightly.yml
  # full-quality copy — the pre-merge gate is the single unit-lcov producer.
  dart test ${conc:+--concurrency=$conc} --tags integration \
    test/cli/jsr_cli_test.dart \
    test/cli/cli_args_jsr_test.dart \
    test/cli/agent_cli_jsr_test.dart \
    --coverage=coverage
}

stage_integration_mock() {
  # Issue #551: the no-key integration legs run on EVERY PR that touches
  # them — MockLlmServer scenarios, no secrets, no network, so they cannot
  # rot silently between releases (#538 class). Real-provider files carry
  # the `llm` tag and stay in the tag-only smoke job; browser-ext owns its
  # own workflow; perf has the #303 per-PR trajectory gate; `pty` marks
  # child-agent-spawn tests (issue #553) — nightly-only, unbounded boot time.
  #
  # TMPDIR normalization (macOS hook parity): several PTY legs assert the
  # status row still shows `· ctx ` — with macOS's per-user temp root
  # (/var/folders/<30 chars>/T/...) the temp cwd eats the whole row width
  # and the assertion fails locally while ubuntu CI (/tmp) is green. Pin
  # the stage to the same short temp root CI has so hook/CI agree.
  echo "🧪 Running no-key integration legs (MockLlmServer)..."
  local conc="${FA_DART_TEST_CONCURRENCY:-$(detect_test_concurrency)}"
  echo "   concurrency: ${conc:-default}"
  #
  # Flake budget (gh-1026): FA_GATE_PTY_RETRIES=N reruns ONLY the failed
  # files, up to N times, before the stage fails. The PTY/grid timing legs
  # are load-sensitive (the gh-1026 class: 3 red 2.5 h gate runs on an
  # unchanged head, a different ambient test red each time, every file
  # green in isolation) — the budget turns one flaky PTY case from a full
  # leg rerun into a minutes-scoped file rerun, mirroring CI's
  # retrigger-recovery behaviour (ci.yml watchdog: ONE retrigger, never a
  # blind rerun). 0 (the default) keeps the single-shot leg below
  # byte-identical. Files come from scripts/gate_failed_targets.py over
  # the dart json file-reporter log; when the log yields no targets
  # (crash before the reporter flushed) the stage fails WITHOUT a rerun —
  # never rerun blind.
  local retries="${FA_GATE_PTY_RETRIES:-0}"
  if [ "$retries" -le 0 ]; then
    TMPDIR="${FA_GATE_TMPDIR:-/tmp}" \
      dart test ${conc:+--concurrency=$conc} test/integration \
      --exclude-tags llm,browser-ext,perf,pty
    return
  fi
  local log="test-results/gate-integration-mock.json"
  mkdir -p test-results
  local targets="test/integration"
  local attempt=0
  while true; do
    attempt=$((attempt + 1))
    if TMPDIR="${FA_GATE_TMPDIR:-/tmp}" \
        dart test ${conc:+--concurrency=$conc} $targets \
        --exclude-tags llm,browser-ext,perf,pty \
        --file-reporter="json:$log"; then
      return 0
    fi
    if [ "$attempt" -gt "$retries" ]; then
      echo "❌ flake budget exhausted ($retries rerun(s)) — integration leg stays red" >&2
      exit 1
    fi
    local failed
    failed=$(python3 scripts/gate_failed_targets.py "$log")
    if [ -z "$failed" ]; then
      echo "   no failed-file targets in $log — not rerunning blind" >&2
      exit 1
    fi
    echo "🔁 flake budget: rerun $attempt/$retries — failed files only:" >&2
    printf '%s\n' "$failed" | sed 's/^/   /' >&2
    targets="$failed"
  done
}

Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. stage_test_core() {
  echo "🧪 Running dart test --coverage (excluding integration tests)..."
  rm -rf coverage
  local conc="${FA_DART_TEST_CONCURRENCY:-$(detect_test_concurrency)}"
  echo "   concurrency: ${conc:-default}"
  dart test ${conc:+--concurrency=$conc} --coverage=coverage --exclude-tags integration
  # gh-1033 (review thread 7 + gate wiring): the fa jsr delegate suites are
  # integration-tagged — the PTY leg's CLI coverage ratchet measures
  # lib/src/cli hits from them — so the unit run above skips them. Their
  # hits must ALSO reach the unit-side lcov consumers (>= 80% ratchet, PR
  # diff-coverage, CRAP: jsr_cli.dart at 0% line coverage reads CRAP 156
  # against the 12.0 ceiling), so the trio runs into the SAME coverage/
  # dir; format_coverage merges the per-isolate files. Keep this list in
  # sync with ci.yml (test-core shard 0); gh-1538 retired the nightly.yml
  # full-quality copy — the pre-merge gate is the single unit-lcov producer.
  dart test ${conc:+--concurrency=$conc} --tags integration \
    test/cli/jsr_cli_test.dart \
    test/cli/cli_args_jsr_test.dart \
    test/cli/agent_cli_jsr_test.dart \
    --coverage=coverage

stage_integration_mock() {
  # Issue #551: the no-key integration legs run on EVERY PR that touches
  # them — MockLlmServer scenarios, no secrets, no network, so they cannot
  # rot silently between releases (#538 class). Real-provider files carry
  # the `llm` tag and stay in the tag-only smoke job; browser-ext owns its
  # own workflow; perf has the #303 per-PR trajectory gate; `pty` marks
  # child-agent-spawn tests (issue #553) — nightly-only, unbounded boot time.
  #
  # TMPDIR normalization (macOS hook parity): several PTY legs assert the
  # status row still shows `· ctx ` — with macOS's per-user temp root
  # (/var/folders/<30 chars>/T/...) the temp cwd eats the whole row width
  # and the assertion fails locally while ubuntu CI (/tmp) is green. Pin
  # the stage to the same short temp root CI has so hook/CI agree.
  echo "🧪 Running no-key integration legs (MockLlmServer)..."
  local conc="${FA_DART_TEST_CONCURRENCY:-$(detect_test_concurrency)}"
  echo "   concurrency: ${conc:-default}"
  #
  # Flake budget (gh-1026): FA_GATE_PTY_RETRIES=N reruns ONLY the failed
  # files, up to N times, before the stage fails. The PTY/grid timing legs
  # are load-sensitive (the gh-1026 class: 3 red 2.5 h gate runs on an
  # unchanged head, a different ambient test red each time, every file
  # green in isolation) — the budget turns one flaky PTY case from a full
  # leg rerun into a minutes-scoped file rerun, mirroring CI's
  # retrigger-recovery behaviour (ci.yml watchdog: ONE retrigger, never a
  # blind rerun). 0 (the default) keeps the single-shot leg below
  # byte-identical. Files come from scripts/gate_failed_targets.py over
  # the dart json file-reporter log; when the log yields no targets
  # (crash before the reporter flushed) the stage fails WITHOUT a rerun —
  # never rerun blind.
  local retries="${FA_GATE_PTY_RETRIES:-0}"
  if [ "$retries" -le 0 ]; then
    TMPDIR="${FA_GATE_TMPDIR:-/tmp}" \
      dart test ${conc:+--concurrency=$conc} test/integration \
      --exclude-tags llm,browser-ext,perf,pty
    return
  fi
  local log="test-results/gate-integration-mock.json"
  mkdir -p test-results
  local targets="test/integration"
  local attempt=0
  while true; do
    attempt=$((attempt + 1))
    if TMPDIR="${FA_GATE_TMPDIR:-/tmp}" \
        dart test ${conc:+--concurrency=$conc} $targets \
        --exclude-tags llm,browser-ext,perf,pty \
        --file-reporter="json:$log"; then
      return 0
    fi
    if [ "$attempt" -gt "$retries" ]; then
      echo "❌ flake budget exhausted ($retries rerun(s)) — integration leg stays red" >&2
      exit 1
    fi
    local failed
    failed=$(python3 scripts/gate_failed_targets.py "$log")
    if [ -z "$failed" ]; then
      echo "   no failed-file targets in $log — not rerunning blind" >&2
      exit 1
    fi
    echo "🔁 flake budget: rerun $attempt/$retries — failed files only:" >&2
    printf '%s\n' "$failed" | sed 's/^/   /' >&2
    targets="$failed"
  done
}

# merge-base == HEAD (a main dispatch, or an already-merged
          # branch) diffs to nothing and the narrowed arms skip. A failed

          # one hides a nightly-only red (the #1309 class).
          if [ -z "$HEAD_REF" ]; then
            HEAD_REF="$(git rev-parse HEAD)"
            BASE_REF="$(git merge-base origin/main "$HEAD_REF" 2>/dev/null || true)"
            if [ -z "$BASE_REF" ]; then
              echo "::warning::merge-base(origin/main, HEAD) failed on the dispatch checkout — failing safe: exzone + locksmoke arms run"
              echo "exzone=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
              echo "locksmoke=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
              echo "installer=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

          # Issue #1267 N1: the macOS exclusion-zone path set. Gated on
          # BOTH pull_request events and SM validation dispatches (the
          # legs below consult these outputs on either event). Context:

              grep -qE '(^flutter_app/lib/apps/|^lib/src/js_ext/|^flutter_app/test/apps/|^flutter_app/test/native_test_guard\.dart$|^flutter_app/pubspec\.yaml$)'; then

stage_test_core() {
  echo "🧪 Running dart test --coverage (excluding integration tests)..."
  rm -rf coverage
  local conc="${FA_DART_TEST_CONCURRENCY:-$(detect_test_concurrency)}"
  echo "   concurrency: ${conc:-default}"
  dart test ${conc:+--concurrency=$conc} --coverage=coverage --exclude-tags integration
  # gh-1033 (review thread 7 + gate wiring): the fa jsr delegate suites are
  # integration-tagged — the PTY leg's CLI coverage ratchet measures
  # lib/src/cli hits from them — so the unit run above skips them. Their
  # hits must ALSO reach the unit-side lcov consumers (>= 80% ratchet, PR
  # diff-coverage, CRAP: jsr_cli.dart at 0% line coverage reads CRAP 156
  # against the 12.0 ceiling), so the trio runs into the SAME coverage/
  # dir; format_coverage merges the per-isolate files. Keep this list in
  # sync with ci.yml (test-core shard 0); gh-1538 retired the nightly.yml
  # full-quality copy — the pre-merge gate is the single unit-lcov producer.
  dart test ${conc:+--concurrency=$conc} --tags integration \
    test/cli/jsr_cli_test.dart \
    test/cli/cli_args_jsr_test.dart \
    test/cli/agent_cli_jsr_test.dart \
    --coverage=coverage
}

stage_integration_mock() {
  # Issue #551: the no-key integration legs run on EVERY PR that touches
  # them — MockLlmServer scenarios, no secrets, no network, so they cannot
  # rot silently between releases (#538 class). Real-provider files carry
  # the `llm` tag and stay in the tag-only smoke job; browser-ext owns its
  # own workflow; perf has the #303 per-PR trajectory gate; `pty` marks
  # child-agent-spawn tests (issue #553) — nightly-only, unbounded boot time.
  #
  # TMPDIR normalization (macOS hook parity): several PTY legs assert the
  # status row still shows `· ctx ` — with macOS's per-user temp root
  # (/var/folders/<30 chars>/T/...) the temp cwd eats the whole row width
  # and the assertion fails locally while ubuntu CI (/tmp) is green. Pin
  # the stage to the same short temp root CI has so hook/CI agree.
  echo "🧪 Running no-key integration legs (MockLlmServer)..."
  local conc="${FA_DART_TEST_CONCURRENCY:-$(detect_test_concurrency)}"
  echo "   concurrency: ${conc:-default}"
  #
  # Flake budget (gh-1026): FA_GATE_PTY_RETRIES=N reruns ONLY the failed
  # files, up to N times, before the stage fails. The PTY/grid timing legs
  # are load-sensitive (the gh-1026 class: 3 red 2.5 h gate runs on an
  # unchanged head, a different ambient test red each time, every file
  # green in isolation) — the budget turns one flaky PTY case from a full
  # leg rerun into a minutes-scoped file rerun, mirroring CI's
  # retrigger-recovery behaviour (ci.yml watchdog: ONE retrigger, never a
  # blind rerun). 0 (the default) keeps the single-shot leg below
  # byte-identical. Files come from scripts/gate_failed_targets.py over
  # the dart json file-reporter log; when the log yields no targets
  # (crash before the reporter flushed) the stage fails WITHOUT a rerun —
  # never rerun blind.
  local retries="${FA_GATE_PTY_RETRIES:-0}"
  if [ "$retries" -le 0 ]; then
    TMPDIR="${FA_GATE_TMPDIR:-/tmp}" \
      dart test ${conc:+--concurrency=$conc} test/integration \
      --exclude-tags llm,browser-ext,perf,pty
    return
  fi
  local log="test-results/gate-integration-mock.json"
  mkdir -p test-results
  local targets="test/integration"
  local attempt=0
  while true; do
    attempt=$((attempt + 1))
    if TMPDIR="${FA_GATE_TMPDIR:-/tmp}" \
        dart test ${conc:+--concurrency=$conc} $targets \
        --exclude-tags llm,browser-ext,perf,pty \
        --file-reporter="json:$log"; then
      return 0
    fi
    if [ "$attempt" -gt "$retries" ]; then
      echo "❌ flake budget exhausted ($retries rerun(s)) — integration leg stays red" >&2
      exit 1
    fi
    local failed
    failed=$(python3 scripts/gate_failed_targets.py "$log")
    if [ -z "$failed" ]; then
      echo "   no failed-file targets in $log — not rerunning blind" >&2
      exit 1
    fi
    echo "🔁 flake budget: rerun $attempt/$retries — failed files only:" >&2
    printf '%s\n' "$failed" | sed 's/^/   /' >&2
    targets="$failed"
  done
}

10:#   PR opened by ai-teammate         → factory, leg=review on the linked

12:#   workflow_dispatch (SM / manual)  → leg pinned by input

14:# ALL loop logic lives in IstiN/dmtools-agents/.github/workflows/
15:# factory-teammate.yml (guard, legs, verdict, sessions, memory). This file
16:# carries only what cannot live in a reusable workflow: the repository
17:# event triggers, the author filter, the PR→issue resolution, the
18:# per-issue concurrency group, and the call itself.
19:#
20:# Secrets (explicit mapping): SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN (required by the factory),

27:run-name: >-
28:  ${{ github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' &&

32:      format('{0} · gh-{1}: {2}',
33:        github.event.action == 'assigned' && '⚒️ dev (assigned handoff)' || 'machine loop',

36:on:
37:  issues:
38:    # assigned only — labeled REMOVED (2026-10-01): every label echo (the dev
39:    # leg's own status:In Development, SM backfills) spawned a queued twin run
40:    # behind the per-issue concurrency group (live dmd gh-317/gh-318); the
41:    # in-run dedupe cannot act — workflow-level concurrency holds the whole
42:    # run pending before any job starts. Leg dispatching is dispatch-only
43:    # (SM workflow_dispatch; manual rework override #544 = dispatch leg=rework).
44:    types: [assigned]
45:  workflow_dispatch:
46:    inputs:
47:      issue:
48:        description: 'Issue number to run the agent on (empty for PR-anchored runs, #687)'
49:        required: false
50:        type: string
51:        default: ''
52:      leg:

55:        type: choice

58:        description: 'Why this dispatch (audit trail, shown in logs)'
59:        required: false
60:        type: string
61:      pr:

63:        required: false
64:        type: string
65:        default: ''

67:# Explicit top-level permissions, minimal read: job-level grants below carry
68:# the real rights (SEC-08 review #849, thread -1oD — a top-level write block
69:# becomes the default for every future job in this workflow). The factory
70:# job's own permissions block mirrors the pinned callee's declared scopes
71:# (factory-teammate.yml declares contents/issues/pull-requests/actions
72:# write): a reusable workflow cannot RAISE rights above the CALLING JOB's
73:# effective grant, so an explicit read-only block ON THE CALLING JOB made
74:# every call fail validation with startup_failure (live bisect,
75:# 2026-09-18) — the job-scoped mirror is the minimal consistent set (SEC-08,
76:# #796).
77:permissions:
78:  contents: read
79:
80:concurrency:
81:  # PR-anchored dispatches (#544/#687) carry no issue — fall back to the pr
82:  # input so each PR keeps its OWN group ('ai-teammate-issue-pr-266');
83:  # without it every PR-anchored run shares the empty group and serializes
84:  # across unrelated PRs.
85:  group: ai-teammate-issue-${{ github.event.issue.number || github.event.inputs.issue || format('pr-{0}', github.event.inputs.pr) }}
86:  cancel-in-progress: false

88:jobs:
89:  # Assignment gate. Runs ONLY when the issue is assigned to `ai-teammate`
90:  # (the human handoff) or on explicit dispatch (SM ticks). Everything else
91:  # exits empty and the factory job is skipped. PRs do NOT trigger this
92:  # workflow: the loop's review/rework legs are driven by SM ticks and
93:  # issue labels, and pull_request-triggered runs of this stub validated
94:  # as startup_failure on PRs #624/#625 (red-X noise with no value).
95:  gate:
96:    if: >-
97:      github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' ||
98:      (github.event_name == 'issues' && contains(github.event.issue.assignees.*.login, 'ai-teammate'))
99:    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04

101:    # It inherits the workflow-level read-only default and must NOT see the
102:    # factory job's write scopes (SEC-08 review, #796).
103:    permissions:
104:      contents: read

107:      leg: ${{ steps.resolve.outputs.leg }}

109:      - name: Resolve target issue and leg for this event
110:        id: resolve
111:        env:
112:          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
113:          EVENT: ${{ github.event_name }}
114:          ACTION: ${{ github.event.action }}
115:          NUMBER: ${{ github.event.number }}
116:          ISSUE_NUMBER: ${{ github.event.issue.number }}
117:        run: |
118:          set -eu
119:          case "$EVENT" in
120:            workflow_dispatch)
121:              # Manual/SM dispatch: inputs flow straight through.
122:              echo "issue=${ISSUE_NUMBER}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"   # empty here; factory takes inputs.issue
123:              echo "leg=" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
124:              ;;
125:            issues)

127:              # handoff) → dev leg; `labeled` (agent:review / agent:rework
128:              # added by the machine itself while assigned) → guard derives.
129:              # POLICY (#693 steering): dev fires ONLY when ai-teammate is
130:              # the sole assignee — any human assignee owns the issue and
131:              # the machine stands by for reviews instead (review paths:
132:              # review-external-once / agent:review on the eventual PR).
133:              if [ "$ACTION" = "assigned" ]; then
134:                HUMAN=$(gh api "repos/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/issues/${ISSUE_NUMBER}" \
135:                  --jq '[.assignees[].login] | map(select(. != "ai-teammate")) | length')
136:                if [ "$HUMAN" = "0" ]; then
137:                  echo "leg=dev" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
138:                else
139:                  echo "leg=" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
140:                  echo "::notice title=machine-standby::issue #${ISSUE_NUMBER} has a human assignee — no dev, review-only"
141:                fi
142:              else
143:                echo "leg=" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
144:              fi
145:              echo "issue=${ISSUE_NUMBER}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
146:              ;;
147:          esac
148:          echo "→ gate done (see outputs)"
149:
150:  factory:
151:    needs: gate
152:    # Dispatch runs carry the target in inputs (gate outputs are empty by
153:    # design there); event runs carry it in gate outputs.
154:    if: needs.gate.result == 'success' && (needs.gate.outputs.issue != '' || github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch')
155:    # Job-scoped grants mirroring the pinned callee's declared scopes (a
156:    # reusable call is capped by the calling job's effective permissions —
157:    # see the top-level comment). Scoped to THIS job so any future job in
158:    # this workflow defaults to the top-level read-only.
159:    permissions:
160:      contents: write         #…

stage_test_core() {
  echo "🧪 Running dart test --coverage (excluding integration tests)..."
  rm -rf coverage
  local conc="${FA_DART_TEST_CONCURRENCY:-$(detect_test_concurrency)}"
  echo "   concurrency: ${conc:-default}"
  dart test ${conc:+--concurrency=$conc} --coverage=coverage --exclude-tags integration
  # gh-1033 (review thread 7 + gate wiring): the fa jsr delegate suites are
  # integration-tagged — the PTY leg's CLI coverage ratchet measures
  # lib/src/cli hits from them — so the unit run above skips them. Their
  # hits must ALSO reach the unit-side lcov consumers (>= 80% ratchet, PR
  # diff-coverage, CRAP: jsr_cli.dart at 0% line coverage reads CRAP 156
  # against the 12.0 ceiling), so the trio runs into the SAME coverage/
  # dir; format_coverage merges the per-isolate files. Keep this list in
  # sync with ci.yml (test-core shard 0); gh-1538 retired the nightly.yml
  # full-quality copy — the pre-merge gate is the single unit-lcov producer.
  dart test ${conc:+--concurrency=$conc} --tags integration \
    test/cli/jsr_cli_test.dart \
    test/cli/cli_args_jsr_test.dart \
    test/cli/agent_cli_jsr_test.dart \
    --coverage=coverage
}

stage_integration_mock() {
  # Issue #551: the no-key integration legs run on EVERY PR that touches
  # them — MockLlmServer scenarios, no secrets, no network, so they cannot
  # rot silently between releases (#538 class). Real-provider files carry
  # the `llm` tag and stay in the tag-only smoke job; browser-ext owns its
  # own workflow; perf has the #303 per-PR trajectory gate; `pty` marks
  # child-agent-spawn tests (issue #553) — nightly-only, unbounded boot time.
  #
  # TMPDIR normalization (macOS hook parity): several PTY legs assert the
  # status row still shows `· ctx ` — with macOS's per-user temp root
  # (/var/folders/<30 chars>/T/...) the temp cwd eats the whole row width
  # and the assertion fails locally while ubuntu CI (/tmp) is green. Pin
  # the stage to the same short temp root CI has so hook/CI agree.
  echo "🧪 Running no-key integration legs (MockLlmServer)..."
  local conc="${FA_DART_TEST_CONCURRENCY:-$(detect_test_concurrency)}"
  echo "   concurrency: ${conc:-default}"
  #
  # Flake budget (gh-1026): FA_GATE_PTY_RETRIES=N reruns ONLY the failed
  # files, up to N times, before the stage fails. The PTY/grid timing legs
  # are load-sensitive (the gh-1026 class: 3 red 2.5 h gate runs on an
  # unchanged head, a different ambient test red each time, every file
  # green in isolation) — the budget turns one flaky PTY case from a full
  # leg rerun into a minutes-scoped file rerun, mirroring CI's
  # retrigger-recovery behaviour (ci.yml watchdog: ONE retrigger, never a
  # blind rerun). 0 (the default) keeps the single-shot leg below
  # byte-identical. Files come from scripts/gate_failed_targets.py over
  # the dart json file-reporter log; when the log yields no targets
  # (crash before the reporter flushed) the stage fails WITHOUT a rerun —
  # never rerun blind.
  local retries="${FA_GATE_PTY_RETRIES:-0}"
  if [ "$retries" -le 0 ]; then
    TMPDIR="${FA_GATE_TMPDIR:-/tmp}" \
      dart test ${conc:+--concurrency=$conc} test/integration \
      --exclude-tags llm,browser-ext,perf,pty
    return
  fi
  local log="test-results/gate-integration-mock.json"
  mkdir -p test-results
  local targets="test/integration"
  local attempt=0
  while true; do
    attempt=$((attempt + 1))
    if TMPDIR="${FA_GATE_TMPDIR:-/tmp}" \
        dart test ${conc:+--concurrency=$conc} $targets \
        --exclude-tags llm,browser-ext,perf,pty \
        --file-reporter="json:$log"; then
      return 0
    fi
    if [ "$attempt" -gt "$retries" ]; then
      echo "❌ flake budget exhausted ($retries rerun(s)) — integration leg stays red" >&2
      exit 1
    fi
    local failed
    failed=$(python3 scripts/gate_failed_targets.py "$log")
    if [ -z "$failed" ]; then
      echo "   no failed-file targets in $log — not rerunning blind" >&2
      exit 1
    fi
    echo "🔁 flake budget: rerun $attempt/$retries — failed files only:" >&2
    printf '%s\n' "$failed" | sed 's/^/   /' >&2
    targets="$failed"
  done
}

[.github/workflows/ai-teammate.yml#D3EC]
1:# AI Teammate — thin stub over the dmtools-agents factory (reusable pack).
2:#
3:# ROLLOUT SCOPE (this phase): the loop reacts ONLY to artifacts authored
4:# by the machine itself — issues opened by `ai-teammate` and PRs opened
5:# by `ai-teammate`. Human-created issues (even labeled/assigned to the
6:# agent) do NOT trigger anything yet; that gate opens in a later phase.
7:#
8:#   issue ASSIGNED to ai-teammate   → factory, leg=dev (fresh handoff)
9:#   issue labeled while assigned     → factory, leg derived by the guard
10:#   PR opened by ai-teammate         → factory, leg=review on the linked
11:#                                      issue (parsed from the PR body)
12:#   workflow_dispatch (SM / manual)  → leg pinned by input
13:#
14:# ALL loop logic lives in IstiN/dmtools-agents/.github/workflows/
15:# factory-teammate.yml (guard, legs, verdict, sessions, memory). This file
16:# carries only what cannot live in a reusable workflow: the repository
17:# event triggers, the author filter, the PR→issue resolution, the
18:# per-issue concurrency group, and the call itself.
19:#
20:# Secrets (explicit mapping): SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN (required by the factory),
21:# ZAI_CODE_KEY, KIMI_REVIEW_KEY (optional provider keys).
22:# Vars: FA_VERSION_MACHINE || FA_VERSION || latest, DMTOOLS_VERSION,
23:# MAX_AUTO_REWORK_ROUNDS.

25:name: 'AI Teammate'
26:
27:run-name: >-
28:  ${{ github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' &&
29:      ((github.event.inputs.pr || '') != '' &&
30:       format('▶ {0} (SM) · pr-{1}', github.event.inputs.leg, github.event.inputs.pr) ||
31:       format('▶ {0} (SM) · gh-{1}', github.event.inputs.leg, github.event.inputs.issue)) ||
32:      format('{0} · gh-{1}: {2}',
33:        github.event.action == 'assigned' && '⚒️ dev (assigned handoff)' || 'machine loop',
34:        github.event.issue.number, github.event.issue.title) }}
35:
36:on:
37:  issues:
38:    # assigned only — labeled REMOVED (2026-10-01): every label echo (the dev
39:    # leg's own status:In Development, SM backfills) spawned a queued twin run
40:    # behind the per-issue concurrency group (live dmd gh-317/gh-318); the
41:    # in-run dedupe cannot act — workflow-level concurrency holds the whole
42:    # run pending before any job starts. Leg dispatching is dispatch-only
43:    # (SM workflow_dispatch; manual rework override #544 = dispatch leg=rework).
44:    types: [assigned]
45:  workflow_dispatch:
46:    inputs:
47:      issue:
48:        description: 'Issue number to run the agent on (empty for PR-anchored runs, #687)'
49:        required: false
50:        type: string
51:        default: ''
52:      leg:
53:        description: 'Which leg to run'
54:        required: true
55:        type: choice
56:        options: [dev, review, rework]
57:      reason:
58:        description: 'Why this dispatch (audit trail, shown in logs)'
59:        required: false
60:        type: string
61:      pr:
62:        description: 'PR number for PR-anchored review runs (#687) — the SM dispatches review with pr instead of issue'
63:        required: false
64:        type: string
65:        default: ''
66:
67:# Explicit top-level permissions, minimal read: job-level grants below carry
68:# the real rights (SEC-08 review #849, thread -1oD — a top-level write block
69:# becomes the default for every future job in this workflow). The factory
70:# job's own permissions block mirrors the pinned callee's declared scopes
71:# (factory-teammate.yml declares contents/issues/pull-requests/actions
72:# write): a reusable workflow cannot RAISE rights above the CALLING JOB's
73:# effective grant, so an explicit read-only block ON THE CALLING JOB made
74:# every call fail validation with startup_failure (live bisect,
75:# 2026-09-18) — the job-scoped mirror is the minimal consistent set (SEC-08,
76:# #796).
77:permissions:
78:  contents: read
79:
80:concurrency:
81:  # PR-anchored dispatches (#544/#687) carry no issue — fall back to the pr
82:  # input so each PR keeps its OWN group ('ai-teammate-issue-pr-266');
83:  # without it every PR-anchored run shares the empty group and serializes
84:  # across unrelated PRs.
85:  group: ai-teammate-issue-${{ github.event.issue.number || github.event.inputs.issue || format('pr-{0}', github.event.inputs.pr) }}
86:  cancel-in-progress: false
87:
88:jobs:
89:  # Assignment gate. Runs ONLY when the issue is assigned to `ai-teammate`
90:  # (the human handoff) or on explicit dispatch (SM ticks). Everything else
91:  # exits empty and the factory job is skipped. PRs do NOT trigger this
92:  # workflow: the loop's review/rework legs are driven by SM ticks and
93:  # issue labels, and pull_request-triggered runs of this stub validated
94:  # as startup_failure on PRs #624/#625 (red-X noise with no value).
95:  gate:
96:    if: >-
97:      github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' ||
98:      (github.event_name == 'issues' && contains(github.event.issue.assignees.*.login, 'ai-teammate'))
99:    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
100:    # Read-only: this job only resolves assignees/inputs and echoes outputs.
101:    # It inherits the workflow-level read-only default and must NOT see the
102:    # factory job's write scopes (SEC-08 review, #796).
103:    permissions:
104:      contents: read
105:    outputs:
106:      issue: ${{ steps.resolve.outputs.issue }}
107:      leg: ${{ steps.resolve.outputs.leg }}
108:    steps:
109:      - name: Resolve target issue and leg for this event
110:        id: resolve
111:        env:
112:          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
113:          EVENT: ${{ github.event_name }}
114:          ACTION: ${{ github.event.action }}
115:          NUMBER: ${{ github.event.number }}
116:          ISSUE_NUMBER: ${{ github.event.issue.number }}
117:        run: |
118:          set -eu
119:          case "$EVENT" in
120:            workflow_dispatch)
121:              # Manual/SM dispatch: inputs flow straight through.
122:              echo "issue=${ISSUE_NUMBER}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"   # empty here; factory takes inputs.issue
123:              echo "leg=" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
124:              ;;
125:            issues)
126:              # Assignment-driven loop: a fresh `assigned` event (human
127:              # handoff) → dev leg; `labeled` (agent:review / agent:rework
128:              # added by the machine itself while assigned) → guard derives.
129:              # POLICY (#693 steering): dev fires ONLY when ai-teammate is
130:              # the sole assignee — any human assignee owns the issue and
131:              # the machine stands by for reviews instead (review paths:
132:              # review-external-once / agent:review on the eventual PR).
133:              if [ "$ACTION" = "assigned" ]; then
134:                HUMAN=$(gh api "repos/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/issues/${ISSUE_NUMBER}" \
135:                  --jq '[.assignees[].login] | map(select(. != "ai-teammate")) | length')
136:                if [ "$HUMAN" = "0" ]; then
137:                  echo "leg=dev" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
138:                else
139:                  echo "leg=" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
140:                  echo "::notice title=machine-standby::issue #${ISSUE_NUMBER} has a human assignee — no dev, review-only"
141:                fi
142:              else
143:                echo "leg=" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
144:              fi
145:              echo "issue=${ISSUE_NUMBER}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
146:              ;;
147:          esac
148:          echo "→ gate done (see outputs)"
149:
150:  factory:
151:    needs: gate
152:    # Dispatch runs carry the target in inputs (gate outputs are empty by
153:    # design there); event runs carry it in gate outputs.
154:    if: needs.gate.result == 'success' && (needs.gate.outputs.issue != '' || github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch')
155:    # Job-scoped grants mirroring the pinned callee's declared scopes (a
156:    # reusable call is capped by the calling job's effective permissions —
157:    # see the top-level comment). Scoped to THIS job so any future job in
158:    # this workflow defaults to the top-level read-only.
159:    permissions:
160:      contents: write         #…

# merge-base == HEAD (a main dispatch, or an already-merged
          # branch) diffs to nothing and the narrowed arms skip. A failed
          # resolve fails SAFE: both arms run unconditioned —
          # over-triggering a rare-path leg costs minutes, under-triggering
          # one hides a nightly-only red (the #1309 class).
          if [ -z "$HEAD_REF" ]; then
            HEAD_REF="$(git rev-parse HEAD)"
            BASE_REF="$(git merge-base origin/main "$HEAD_REF" 2>/dev/null || true)"
            if [ -z "$BASE_REF" ]; then
              echo "::warning::merge-base(origin/main, HEAD) failed on the dispatch checkout — failing safe: exzone + locksmoke arms run"
              echo "exzone=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
              echo "locksmoke=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
              echo "installer=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
              exit 0
            fi
          fi
          # Issue #1267 N1: the macOS exclusion-zone path set. Gated on
          # BOTH pull_request events and SM validation dispatches (the
          # legs below consult these outputs on either event). Context:
          # the ubuntu flutter-tests leg runs this family but every
          # engine-dependent test SKIPS there (native_test_guard.dart finds
          # no QuickJS .so on a bare runner); they truly execute only on
          # macOS — the hole #1309 escaped through (gh-1307). The issue's
          # packages/js_widget_runtime/** is an EXTERNAL repo now, so its
          # bumps arrive via the flutter_app/pubspec.yaml pin.
          if git diff --name-only "$BASE_REF" "$HEAD_REF" |
              grep -qE '(^flutter_app/lib/apps/|^lib/src/js_ext/|^flutter_app/test/apps/|^flutter_app/test/native_test_guard\.dart$|^flutter_app/pubspec\.yaml$)'; then
            echo "exzone=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi
          # Issue #1267 N2 (AC2): the lockfile-refresh vector — resolution
          # floats transitive deps to latest-compatible, and the breaking
          # arrival (#1265: a transitive flutter_inappwebview) lands as a
          # flutter_app/pubspec.lock diff with nothing else changed. The
          # flutter-app-lock-smoke legs are the pre-merge net; PRs not
          # touching the lockfile never pay for them.
          if git diff --name-only "$BASE_REF" "$HEAD_REF" |
              grep -qE '^flutter_app/pubspec\.lock$'; then

          # sh artifact under site/ and the generator that renders them.

stage_test_core() {
  echo "🧪 Running dart test --coverage (excluding integration tests)..."
  rm -rf coverage
  local conc="${FA_DART_TEST_CONCURRENCY:-$(detect_test_concurrency)}"
  echo "   concurrency: ${conc:-default}"
  dart test ${conc:+--concurrency=$conc} --coverage=coverage --exclude-tags integration
  # gh-1033 (review thread 7 + gate wiring): the fa jsr delegate suites are
  # integration-tagged — the PTY leg's CLI coverage ratchet measures
  # lib/src/cli hits from them — so the unit run above skips them. Their
  # hits must ALSO reach the unit-side lcov consumers (>= 80% ratchet, PR
  # diff-coverage, CRAP: jsr_cli.dart at 0% line coverage reads CRAP 156
  # against the 12.0 ceiling), so the trio runs into the SAME coverage/
  # dir; format_coverage merges the per-isolate files. Keep this list in
  # sync with ci.yml (test-core shard 0); gh-1538 retired the nightly.yml
  # full-quality copy — the pre-merge gate is the single unit-lcov producer.
  dart test ${conc:+--concurrency=$conc} --tags integration \
    test/cli/jsr_cli_test.dart \
    test/cli/cli_args_jsr_test.dart \
    test/cli/agent_cli_jsr_test.dart \
    --coverage=coverage
}

stage_integration_mock() {
  # Issue #551: the no-key integration legs run on EVERY PR that touches
  # them — MockLlmServer scenarios, no secrets, no network, so they cannot
  # rot silently between releases (#538 class). Real-provider files carry
  # the `llm` tag and stay in the tag-only smoke job; browser-ext owns its
  # own workflow; perf has the #303 per-PR trajectory gate; `pty` marks
  # child-agent-spawn tests (issue #553) — nightly-only, unbounded boot time.
  #
  # TMPDIR normalization (macOS hook parity): several PTY legs assert the
  # status row still shows `· ctx ` — with macOS's per-user temp root
  # (/var/folders/<30 chars>/T/...) the temp cwd eats the whole row width
  # and the assertion fails locally while ubuntu CI (/tmp) is green. Pin
  # the stage to the same short temp root CI has so hook/CI agree.
  echo "🧪 Running no-key integration legs (MockLlmServer)..."
  local conc="${FA_DART_TEST_CONCURRENCY:-$(detect_test_concurrency)}"
  echo "   concurrency: ${conc:-default}"
  #
  # Flake budget (gh-1026): FA_GATE_PTY_RETRIES=N reruns ONLY the failed
  # files, up to N times, before the stage fails. The PTY/grid timing legs
  # are load-sensitive (the gh-1026 class: 3 red 2.5 h gate runs on an
  # unchanged head, a different ambient test red each time, every file
  # green in isolation) — the budget turns one flaky PTY case from a full
  # leg rerun into a minutes-scoped file rerun, mirroring CI's
  # retrigger-recovery behaviour (ci.yml watchdog: ONE retrigger, never a
  # blind rerun). 0 (the default) keeps the single-shot leg below
  # byte-identical. Files come from scripts/gate_failed_targets.py over
  # the dart json file-reporter log; when the log yields no targets
  # (crash before the reporter flushed) the stage fails WITHOUT a rerun —
  # never rerun blind.
  local retries="${FA_GATE_PTY_RETRIES:-0}"
  if [ "$retries" -le 0 ]; then
    TMPDIR="${FA_GATE_TMPDIR:-/tmp}" \
      dart test ${conc:+--concurrency=$conc} test/integration \
      --exclude-tags llm,browser-ext,perf,pty
    return
  fi
  local log="test-results/gate-integration-mock.json"
  mkdir -p test-results
  local targets="test/integration"
  local attempt=0
  while true; do
    attempt=$((attempt + 1))
    if TMPDIR="${FA_GATE_TMPDIR:-/tmp}" \
        dart test ${conc:+--concurrency=$conc} $targets \
        --exclude-tags llm,browser-ext,perf,pty \
        --file-reporter="json:$log"; then
      return 0
    fi
    if [ "$attempt" -gt "$retries" ]; then
      echo "❌ flake budget exhausted ($retries rerun(s)) — integration leg stays red" >&2
      exit 1
    fi
    local failed
    failed=$(python3 scripts/gate_failed_targets.py "$log")
    if [ -z "$failed" ]; then
      echo "   no failed-file targets in $log — not rerunning blind" >&2
      exit 1
    fi
    echo "🔁 flake budget: rerun $attempt/$retries — failed files only:" >&2
    printf '%s\n' "$failed" | sed 's/^/   /' >&2
    targets="$failed"
  done
}

93:  # issue labels, and pull_request-triggered runs of this stub validated

135:                  --jq '[.assignees[].login] | map(select(. != "ai-teammate")) | length')

137:                  echo "leg=dev" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
138:                else
139:                  echo "leg=" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
140:                  echo "::notice title=machine-standby::issue #${ISSUE_NUMBER} has a human assignee — no dev, review-only"
141:                fi
142:              else
143:                echo "leg=" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
144:              fi
145:              echo "issue=${ISSUE_NUMBER}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
146:              ;;
147:          esac
148:          echo "→ gate done (see outputs)"

151:    needs: gate
152:    # Dispatch runs carry the target in inputs (gate outputs are empty by
153:    # design there); event runs carry it in gate outputs.
154:    if: needs.gate.result == 'success' && (needs.gate.outputs.issue != '' || github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch')
155:    # Job-scoped grants mirroring the pinned callee's declared scopes (a

158:    # this workflow defaults to the top-level read-only.

stage_test_core() {
  echo "🧪 Running dart test --coverage (excluding integration tests)..."
  rm -rf coverage
  local conc="${FA_DART_TEST_CONCURRENCY:-$(detect_test_concurrency)}"
  echo "   concurrency: ${conc:-default}"
  dart test ${conc:+--concurrency=$conc} --coverage=coverage --exclude-tags integration
  # gh-1033 (review thread 7 + gate wiring): the fa jsr delegate suites are
  # integration-tagged — the PTY leg's CLI coverage ratchet measures
  # lib/src/cli hits from them — so the unit run above skips them. Their
  # hits must ALSO reach the unit-side lcov consumers (>= 80% ratchet, PR
  # diff-coverage, CRAP: jsr_cli.dart at 0% line coverage reads CRAP 156
  # against the 12.0 ceiling), so the trio runs into the SAME coverage/
  # dir; format_coverage merges the per-isolate files. Keep this list in
  # sync with ci.yml (test-core shard 0); gh-1538 retired the nightly.yml
  # full-quality copy — the pre-merge gate is the single unit-lcov producer.
  dart test ${conc:+--concurrency=$conc} --tags integration \
    test/cli/jsr_cli_test.dart \
    test/cli/cli_args_jsr_test.dart \
    test/cli/agent_cli_jsr_test.dart \
    --coverage=coverage
}

stage_integration_mock() {
  # Issue #551: the no-key integration legs run on EVERY PR that touches
  # them — MockLlmServer scenarios, no secrets, no network, so they cannot
  # rot silently between releases (#538 class). Real-provider files carry
  # the `llm` tag and stay in the tag-only smoke job; browser-ext owns its
  # own workflow; perf has the #303 per-PR trajectory gate; `pty` marks
  # child-agent-spawn tests (issue #553) — nightly-only, unbounded boot time.
  #
  # TMPDIR normalization (macOS hook parity): several PTY legs assert the
  # status row still shows `· ctx ` — with macOS's per-user temp root
  # (/var/folders/<30 chars>/T/...) the temp cwd eats the whole row width
  # and the assertion fails locally while ubuntu CI (/tmp) is green. Pin
  # the stage to the same short temp root CI has so hook/CI agree.
  echo "🧪 Running no-key integration legs (MockLlmServer)..."
  local conc="${FA_DART_TEST_CONCURRENCY:-$(detect_test_concurrency)}"
  echo "   concurrency: ${conc:-default}"
  #
  # Flake budget (gh-1026): FA_GATE_PTY_RETRIES=N reruns ONLY the failed
  # files, up to N times, before the stage fails. The PTY/grid timing legs
  # are load-sensitive (the gh-1026 class: 3 red 2.5 h gate runs on an
  # unchanged head, a different ambient test red each time, every file
  # green in isolation) — the budget turns one flaky PTY case from a full
  # leg rerun into a minutes-scoped file rerun, mirroring CI's
  # retrigger-recovery behaviour (ci.yml watchdog: ONE retrigger, never a
  # blind rerun). 0 (the default) keeps the single-shot leg below
  # byte-identical. Files come from scripts/gate_failed_targets.py over
  # the dart json file-reporter log; when the log yields no targets
  # (crash before the reporter flushed) the stage fails WITHOUT a rerun —
  # never rerun blind.
  local retries="${FA_GATE_PTY_RETRIES:-0}"
  if [ "$retries" -le 0 ]; then
    TMPDIR="${FA_GATE_TMPDIR:-/tmp}" \
      dart test ${conc:+--concurrency=$conc} test/integration \
      --exclude-tags llm,browser-ext,perf,pty
    return
  fi
  local log="test-results/gate-integration-mock.json"
  mkdir -p test-results
  local targets="test/integration"
  local attempt=0
  while true; do
    attempt=$((attempt + 1))
    if TMPDIR="${FA_GATE_TMPDIR:-/tmp}" \
        dart test ${conc:+--concurrency=$conc} $targets \
        --exclude-tags llm,browser-ext,perf,pty \
        --file-reporter="json:$log"; then
      return 0
    fi
    if [ "$attempt" -gt "$retries" ]; then
      echo "❌ flake budget exhausted ($retries rerun(s)) — integration leg stays red" >&2
      exit 1
    fi
    local failed
    failed=$(python3 scripts/gate_failed_targets.py "$log")
    if [ -z "$failed" ]; then
      echo "   no failed-file targets in $log — not rerunning blind" >&2
      exit 1
    fi
    echo "🔁 flake budget: rerun $attempt/$retries — failed files only:" >&2
    printf '%s\n' "$failed" | sed 's/^/   /' >&2
    targets="$failed"
  done
}
